correctness.rationale: Chow–Slattery Theorem 1.1 gives a valid Zeckendorf-gap formula; substitution produces the stated even/odd two-coordinate updates and terminal expression. Every noncapped update increases A, while an A>k state has a uniquely summable even-gap-2 tail if q=k. The resulting polynomial recursion gives rational cutoff counts and an affine law; an initial gap of 2k proves the positive leading coefficient. A separate descending-index knapsack program checked all 121393 integers and 25 levels through index L=24, independently of the symbolic recursion. The computations corroborate, rather than prove, the infinite quantifiers.

The pointwise formula permits this new deduction but does not directly imply the theorem without the truncation argument; aggregation of moments does not recover it.

originality.rationale: The nearest original literature establishes pointwise Zeckendorf evaluation, aggregate moments, local multiplicative patches and global sum growth, not the exact distribution of single fixed values over Fibonacci cutoffs. A direct finite polynomial recursion for every positive target k and its bounded-error logarithmic law is a distinct theorem; searches found no stronger published statement implying it. This is best-knowledge priority, not a guarantee against overlooked older automata results.
residual_risks: A 2001 Berstel-style automaton or related older Fibonacci-representation study may contain an equivalent but differently formulated fixed-value enumeration; exhaustive priority certification is not claimed.
Zhou manuscript and older work by Carlitz, Robbins, and Shallit were not inspected in full.
The finite computational tests do not replace the proof or a later external validation.

value.rationale: Classifying the countably infinite thin fibers of the erratic Fibonacci partition function is mathematically motivated by the contrast with its large moment growth. The theorem gives an exact rational series uniformly in every fixed positive target value, eventual affine cutoff counts, and a bounded-error logarithmic counting constant; it is not a table recomputation or one-off small cutoff. The k=12 example supplies an exact nontrivial instance, while the general transfer mechanism is the principal value.
